executive_notes: Definitive full-year scope: 2027, 2028, 2029 and 2030 (48 months). Keep only a separate minimal 2026 bridge for current-date and 2026/2027 school context.
The legal truth changed THREE DAYS before the research date. Use ZPDPD NPB11 effective 17 October 2026 rather than stale GOV.SI summary.
State holiday and work-free are independent booleans. 31 October is listed in Article 2 as another work-free day; avoid treating all work-free dates as Article 1 state holidays.
23 individual legal dates each year: 17 state-holiday dates (15 named holidays) plus 6 other work-free dates. There are 15 statutory work-free dates including Easter Sunday and Pentecost Sunday.
Sunday holiday does not transfer to the next working day, explicitly ZPDPD Article 3. Do not create observed-Monday holidays. Saturday dates also have no substitute-day rule in the Act.
Workdays in this file assume Monday–Friday and remove only statutory work-free dates. They do not model shift work, annual leave, local closures or an individual employment agreement.

School holidays 2026/2027 are verified. Official 2027/2028, 2028/2029, 2029/2030 and 2030/2031 dates were not found on the Ministry pages as of research. Publish an honest awaiting-publication state; do not extrapolate regional winter breaks.

The booleans on an observance describe that observance’s own legal status. A cultural or international observance can coincide with a separate legal work-free date; combine date-level flags with OR. Example: World Bee Day and Pentecost both fall on 20 May 2029.
2030 fixed holidays follow the current ZPDPD law, not a claim that legislation cannot change before 2030. Reverify the source during implementation and data refreshes.

editorial.quality_rule: Use 40 substantive evergreen pages with year tables. Do not create empty year variants or unsupported event-program details. Historical copy needs a topic-specific primary source beyond the date/status law.

astronomy.seasons_2029_status: API retrieval failed; not copied or invented. Fetch https://aa.usno.navy.mil/api/seasons?year=2029 before publishing exact times.
implementation_notes: USNO moon phase times are Universal Time: convert every instant to Europe/Ljubljana, including date rollover.
Do not use USNO dst=true for Slovenia: the documented flag implements U.S. DST rules. Request UTC and convert with IANA timezone data.
A phase moment is global; its displayed civil date depends on timezone. Sunrise, sunset, moonrise and moonset are location-specific.
ARSO 2026 tide booklet is an excellent Slovenian authority for methodology and Koper; it is not a Ljubljana sunrise data feed.
ARSO attributes moon phases to Astronomsko geofizikalni observatorij Golovec, Univerza v Ljubljani. No 2027–2030 ARSO ephemeris was verified in this research.
Label algorithmic sunrise/sunset as izračun and disclose city/coordinates; do not claim official ARSO values unless imported and checked.
Do not present moon phases as proven causes of health, personality, gardening outcomes or luck.
astronomy.seasons_2030_status: Official USNO seasons endpoint retrieval failed. No exact 2030 equinox/solstice timestamps have been inserted. Retrieve and verify primary ephemeris data before publishing exact moments; do not extrapolate 2027/2028 times.

astronomy.astronomy_not_astrology_note: The 2030 lunar module concerns calculated astronomical phase instants and location-dependent sunrise/sunset. Do not convert these into predictions about health, personality, luck or gardening outcomes. Such interpretations are outside the astronomical source data and the requested factual calendar scope.

Use Europe/Ljubljana for today, day boundaries and astronomical local-time presentation, regardless of browser device timezone.
